pull.title: process: include deputies in README Owner entries

labels.name: Proposed BIP modification

events.message: script: buildtable checks deputy inclusion in readme
bip3: clarify deputy inclusion in readme owner entry
script, refactor: rename authors to owners where relevant

events.body:
The change here also enforces the grouping order {authors, deputies} in the readme. I think this makes sense.

```diff
 | [[bip-0375.mediawiki|375]]
 | Applications
 | Sending Silent Payments with PSBTs
-| Andrew Toth, Ava Chow, josibake, macgyver
+| Andrew Toth, Ava Chow, macgyver, josibake
 | Specification
 | Draft
 |-
 ```

```
$ ./scripts/diffcheck.sh                              
--- scripts/diffcheck.expected	2026-11-01 15:51:21
+++ /var/folders/bz/mn3hr6td37bczwp7j89frs4w0000gn/T/tmp.7GxoGhxTOS/after.diff	2026-11-09 13:37:54
+< | Andrew Toth, Ava Chow, macgyver, josibake
+> | Andrew Toth, Ava Chow, josibake, macgyver
```

comments.body: Perhaps the `$authors` variable should now also be renamed to `$owners` to better express the shifted context.

I’d prefer if both the checks are of the same shape and I don’t mind the belt and suspenders here of checking the same thing twice. Even though that might make it easier to introduce a discrepancy in the future, I don’t anticipate that a regex for Name + Email would be modified frequently.

So, if we decided to go this way, I would suggest that we apply the same modification to the Authors check. It would however make more sense to me to just replace this script with one in a language that’s not “write-only” such as Python.
Good idea, added a refactor commit for the renaming.
Agree on same shape and keeping the check. LMK if you were thinking of a further change at this time.

No action necessary:
I was briefly wondering if `$owners` can even be empty here, given that the Authors header is required. I came to the conclusion that it could be, if Deputies were listed before Authors (which would then later fail on the order check). So, this should stay as is.
